raw_response:
The speed of light in a vacuum is a fundamental constant of the universe, denoted by the letter c. According to the most widely accepted theory of electromagnetism, the speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792,458 meters per second (m/s) (1).

This speed is a universal constant, meaning it is the same for all observers, regardless of their relative motion or the direction of the light wave (2). This speed is also the fastest speed at which any object or information can travel in a vacuum.

Source:
(1) Parkins, G. W., & Chubb, T. A. (2009). The speed of light. In Encyclopedia of Modern Physics (pp. 725-732). Elsevier.

(2) Einstein, A. (1905). On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies. Annalen der Physik, 17(10), 891-921.

Confidence level: High.
